name: Single-Cell Hall House
description: One room, with a hearth, and everything else subordinate to it. This is the irreducible house and the ancestor of most of the others in this catalogue: put a partition in it and you have hall and parlor, put a passage beside it and you have a side-hall plan, build a second one across a breezeway and you have a dogtrot. The single cell is not a small version of a bigger diagram - it is a complete one, in which the hall is kitchen, dining room, parlour and often bedroom at once, and the only rooms that separate out are the ones that must: a store, a stair to the loft, and later a bathroom. Its planning question is not how to arrange rooms but how to arrange a single room so that four uses can share it, which is what the hearth wall and the door position do.

rooms.name: Hall
rooms.note: The house. Entered directly from outside with no lobby of any kind, which is what circulation_parti 'none-direct-entry' means and why this parti has no hall room in the Georgian sense - this IS the hall, in the older meaning the catalogue's rooms/hall.json carries as 'houseplace'.

rooms.name: Store
rooms.note: The first thing to separate out of the single cell, because food needs to be cool and the hall is the warmest place in the building.

rooms.name: Chamber
rooms.note: The second thing to separate out, and the step that turns this type into hall-and-parlor. Optional on purpose: the pure single cell has none, and a brief that needs two of these has asked for a different diagram.

rooms.name: Bath
rooms.note: Wholly unhistoric - the type's sanitation was a privy at the end of the garden, which rooms/privy.json carries - and wholly non-negotiable in a contemporary brief. Placed off the hall because there is nowhere else for it to be.

rooms.name: Loft Stair
rooms.note: A ladder stair or a winder in the corner beside the hearth, taking whatever space is left. In the true single cell it is furniture rather than a room.

scaling.note: min_bay_count is 1, and this parti is the reason that field exists. massings/catalog.json gives this type 250-500 sf and '1-2' bays; every other diagram in the catalogue floors at 3, and compose.py's footprint() used to enforce that floor for everything - which did not merely inflate a one-room house, it declared it lot-infeasible and dropped it before scoring. The type grows by adding a second pen (double-pen), by adding one across an open passage (dogtrot), or upward into the loft - never by widening, because a single cell wider than about 20 ft cannot be spanned by the timber it was built with.

trades_away: Nearly everything a contemporary brief assumes. There is no privacy gradient worth the name - the bath and the chamber open off the room the whole household occupies - no separation of cooking from sitting, no circulation at all, and no possibility of a second bedroom without becoming a different type. What it buys is the cheapest, warmest, most easily built house in this catalogue, and the only one a family could raise in a season with the timber off its own ground.

editorial: the room list is the type reduced to what a contemporary brief will accept, and the bath says so
